findings.claim: oneLine changes the bytes of the error, not only its line breaks. It rebuilds the text with `for _, r := range text` and `b.WriteRune(r)`. In Go, ranging over a string turns each byte that is not valid UTF-8 into utf8.RuneError, and WriteRune writes that as the 3 bytes of U+FFFD. Before this change the hook printed the error's bytes as they were (`%v`). Now any invalid byte in the text is replaced. That includes a working directory or a stored-result path with a non-UTF-8 name (reviewPath's `cannot determine the working directory`, a refusal naming a file) and raw git stderr. The printed line then no longer names the real path. No test covers text that is not UTF-8; the oneLine table has only ASCII cases. A byte loop that touches only '\r' and '\n' would keep every other byte.

oneLine treats only '\r' and '\n' as line breaks. Vertical tab, form feed, NEL (U+0085) and the Unicode line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029) pass through unchanged. Some terminals and log viewers break a line on these, so text from an outside source (git stderr wrapped by gitexec, a panic value) can still show as more than one line. That breaks the doc's promise of 'one line on stderr, whatever line breaks its text holds' (review_stop_hook.go:23). I could not show that real input reaches this, so it is a SUGGESTION. The table in TestOneLineJoinsTheLinesOfAText pins only CR and LF.

A refusal is remembered under refusedKey(refusal.Error()), a hash of its whole text. If one stored file keeps failing but the error text differs from stop to stop (for example, it carries git or filesystem stderr with a temporary path, a PID or a time in it), each stop sees a new key. The refusal is then named again at every stop, which -2 F4 was meant to stop, and one new refused- marker is written to the session store per stop. L72 assumes these markers are 'bounded by the distinct refusal texts of a session'; that holds only if the texts stay the same. Neither M11 nor M3 pins a refusal whose text changes. Keying on the stored file's name (feature, name) instead of the full text would make the count independent of the text. I did not show which refusal texts can vary, so it is a SUGGESTION.
